blogs.title: How to Choose the Right BMS for Your Battery Pack
blogs.author: NexEV Team
blogs.description: A Battery Management System protects, balances and monitors your cells. Here's how to match the right BMS to your pack's voltage, current and chemistry.

content.text: The Battery Management System (BMS) is the brain of every lithium pack. It prevents over-charge, over-discharge, over-current and short circuits, and it keeps individual cells balanced so the whole pack ages evenly. Picking the wrong BMS is the single most common mistake we see from first-time builders.
1. Match the cell count (S rating)
A BMS is rated in series groups: 1S, 2S, 3S and so on. This must exactly match how many cell groups you wire in series. A 3-series Li-ion pack (nominal 11.1V) needs a 3S BMS — never a 2S or 4S.
2. Size the continuous current
Add up the maximum current your load draws and add 20-30% headroom. A motor that pulls 8A continuous is comfortable on a 10A BMS, not a 8A one. Undersized boards overheat and trip.

items: 1S 3A — small gadgets, sensors, LED lights
2S 8A — power banks, small tools, boost packs
3S 10A — 12V backup, routers, e-bike accessories

content.text: 3. Confirm the chemistry
Li-ion / Li-po boards cut off around 4.2V per cell; LiFePO4 boards cut off near 3.65V. Using a Li-ion BMS on a LiFePO4 pack will over-charge and damage it.
When in doubt, size up on current and match the S-rating exactly. The cells will thank you with years of service.

blogs.title: 18650 vs 21700: Which Lithium Cell Is Right for Your Build?
blogs.author: NexEV Team
blogs.description: The two most popular cylindrical cells compared on capacity, current, cost and pack design — so you can pick the format that fits your project.

content.text: 18650 and 21700 are named after their dimensions in millimetres. The 18650 is 18mm x 65mm; the 21700 is 21mm x 70mm. That small size difference changes a lot about how your pack performs.
Capacity and energy density
21700 cells typically store 4000-5000mAh versus 2500-3500mAh for 18650. For the same pack voltage, fewer 21700 cells deliver the same range, which simplifies wiring and spot-welding.
Current handling
21700 cells generally sustain higher continuous discharge, making them the better choice for high-drain applications such as scooters and power tools.

items: Choose 18650 for compact builds and the widest cell selection
Choose 21700 for maximum range and high current
Never mix formats or brands inside one pack

content.text: Both formats spot-weld the same way with pure-nickel strip. NexEV stocks holders and nickel for both — see the shop for current options.

blogs.title: Spot Welding Nickel Strips: A Beginner's Guide
blogs.author: NexEV Team
blogs.description: Soldering directly to cells damages them. Spot welding is the safe, professional way to build a pack. Here's the workflow from strip to finished pack.

content.text: Heat is the enemy of lithium cells. A soldering iron held against a cell terminal for too long degrades the internal chemistry. Spot welding delivers a high-current pulse for milliseconds, bonding nickel to the terminal without cooking the cell.
What you need

items: A spot welder (battery-powered or mains)
Pure-nickel or nickel-plated strip sized to your current
Cell holders to keep alignment
Kapton tape and barley paper for insulation

content.text: The basic workflow

Lay your cells in holders, place the nickel strip across the terminals, and fire two weld points per joint for redundancy. Tug-test every weld — a good weld tears the nickel before it lifts off the cell.
Two welds per joint, always tug-test. A pack is only as reliable as its weakest connection.
Finish with insulation rings on the positive ends and barley paper over the pack face before heat-shrinking. This prevents shorts that can be catastrophic.

blogs.title: Converting Your Scooter to Electric: Where to Start
blogs.author: NexEV Team
blogs.description: Thinking of building an e-scooter? This roadmap covers motor sizing, battery voltage, the controller, and the components you'll source from NexEV.

content.text: An electric conversion comes down to four systems working together: the motor, the battery, the controller and the throttle. Get the voltage right across all four and the rest is assembly.
Pick your voltage first
Everything else follows from system voltage. A 36V system (10S) is common for light scooters; 48V (13S) gives more speed and efficiency. Your motor, controller and charger must all match this number.
Size the battery
Range depends on watt-hours. Multiply pack voltage by amp-hours: a 48V 15Ah pack stores 720Wh, roughly 30-40km of real-world range depending on rider weight and terrain.

items: Motor: hub or mid-drive, matched to system voltage
Battery: built from 18650/21700 with a matching BMS
Controller: rated for peak motor current
Wiring: XT60/XT90 connectors, correct gauge

blogs.title: Lithium Battery Safety: 7 Rules Every Builder Should Know
blogs.author: NexEV Team
blogs.description: Lithium packs are safe when built correctly. Follow these seven non-negotiable rules to protect yourself, your build and the people around you.

content.text: Most lithium incidents trace back to a handful of avoidable mistakes. Internalise these rules before you weld your first cell.

items: Never solder directly to cells — spot weld instead
Always fit a correctly-rated BMS
Match cell brand, capacity and age within a pack
Insulate positive terminals with rings and barley paper
Use a charger rated for your exact pack voltage and chemistry
Fuse the main discharge lead
Charge on a non-flammable surface and never unattended overnight

content.text: If a cell gets hot or swells
Stop immediately, disconnect if safe to do so, and move the pack to a fireproof location outdoors. A swelling cell is venting — it will not recover and must be retired.
A few rupees of insulation and a fuse are the cheapest insurance you will ever buy.

blogs.title: Picking the Correct Charger for 1S / 2S / 3S Packs
blogs.author: NexEV Team
blogs.description: Voltage, current and connector — the three things that must line up between your charger and your pack. A quick reference for small lithium builds.

content.text: A charger that mismatches your pack is at best useless and at worst dangerous. Three numbers must agree: voltage, current and connector type.
Charge voltage

items: 1S Li-ion charges to 4.2V (TP4057 Type-C is ideal)
2S charges to 8.4V
3S charges to 12.6V

content.text: Charge current
A safe default is 0.5C — half the pack's amp-hour rating. A 2Ah pack charges happily at 1A. Higher currents reduce lifespan and add heat.
